# Berlin Rental Dispute Checklist

A calm, practical tenant-rights checklist for a deposit dispute over minor wall scuffs. I’m assuming you want something you can use immediately in writing, without escalating the tone.

## What to Gather Before You Reply

- **Lease agreement** showing the move-in date: **2025-11-01** and end date: **2026-03-31**
- **Handover protocol / move-in inspection report** from when you received the apartment
- **Move-out inspection report** if one was done
- **Deposit payment proof** and any written deposit terms
- **Photos/videos** of the walls at move-in and move-out, if available
- **All written messages** with the landlord or property manager
- **Repair invoices or estimates** they say justify the deduction
- **Any witness notes** if someone saw the apartment condition at move-in or move-out

## Questions to Ask the Landlord

- What exact damage is being claimed, and where is it located?
- Is the issue listed in the move-in or move-out protocol?
- Why is the deduction considered more than normal wear and tear?
- What is the exact amount being withheld from the deposit?
- Can you send a **line-item breakdown** with dates, photos, and invoices?
- Was any repainting or repair actually completed, and by whom?
- If the deduction is for wall scuffs only, how do you separate normal use from damage?
- When will the undisputed part of the deposit be returned?

## Practical Tenant Checklist for a Calm Response

- Keep the message factual and brief
- Ask for a **written, itemized explanation**
- Request supporting documents before agreeing to any deduction
- Do not admit liability for “damage” if it may be normal wear
- Keep copies of everything you send and receive
- Set a reasonable deadline for reply, such as **7–14 days**
- If needed, consider contacting a local tenant association or legal advice service

## Short Message Template

### German
Hallo,

vielen Dank für Ihre Nachricht.
Bitte senden Sie mir eine **schriftliche, itemisierte Erklärung** für den vorgeschlagenen Einbehalt aus der Kaution wegen der kleinen Wandspuren.

Bitte fügen Sie, wenn möglich, auch folgende Unterlagen bei:
- eine genaue Beschreibung der beanstandeten Stellen
- Fotos
- die Übergabeprotokolle
- Rechnungen oder Kostenvoranschläge

Aus meiner Sicht handelt es sich um geringe Gebrauchsspuren. Ich bitte daher auch um Rückzahlung des unstrittigen Teils der Kaution.

Vielen Dank und freundliche Grüße
[Ihr Name]

### English
Hello,

thank you for your message.
Please send me a **written, itemized explanation** for the proposed deduction from the deposit regarding the minor wall scuffs.

If possible, please also include:
- a precise description of the alleged issue
- photos
- the move-in and move-out inspection reports
- invoices or repair estimates

From my perspective, these appear to be minor signs of normal use. I therefore also request repayment of the undisputed part of the deposit.

Thank you and kind regards,
[Your Name]

## Quick Actions

- Consumer advice center: https://www.verbraucherzentrale.de/
